ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the equilateral triangle $ABC$, $BD$ is the median to the side $AC$, and through point $D$, $DE \perp BC$ at point $E$. If $AB=2$, then what is the length of $CE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given: $\because$ $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle, $AB=2$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ABC = \angle C = 60^\circ$, $AB = BC = AC = 2$,\\
Also $\because$ $BD$ is the median to side $AC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DBC = 30^\circ$, $\angle BDC = 90^\circ$, $DC = 1$,\\
Also $\because$ $DE \perp BC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle EDC = 30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $EC = \frac{1}{2} DC = \boxed{\frac{1}{2}}$.

BD is the median on side AC, so D is the midpoint of AC, DC=1; in an equilateral triangle, the median from vertex B to the opposite side AC is also an altitude, therefore in triangle BDC, DC lies along AC, BC lies along CB, and ∠DCE=∠ACB=60°. Also because DE ⟂ BC, triangle DCE is a right triangle at E. Thus triangle DCE is a 30°-60°-90° triangle, with hypotenuse DC=1, and the short right-angle side CE corresponds to 30°, equal to half of the hypotenuse. Therefore CE=1/2.
